title: Vite
description: How Vite serves native ESM in development, builds with Rollup, and handles env variables, aliases, and proxies.

data.text: Vite (French for "fast") skips bundling during development. The browser requests modules over native ESM and Vite transforms them on demand, so a cold start is measured in milliseconds regardless of app size.

Two different engines: the dev server uses esbuild for fast TypeScript/JSX transformation plus native ESM for module loading; `vite build` uses Rollup to produce an optimised production bundle. This is why dev-only warnings and production output can differ.

data.caption: Vite uses different engines for dev and build
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Source files] --> B{Command}
    B -->|vite dev| C[esbuild transforms per module]
    C --> D[Native ESM over HTTP]
    D --> E[Hot module replacement]
    B -->|vite build| F[Rollup graph]
    F --> G[Tree-shaken hashed assets]

data.caption: vite.config.ts — aliases, proxy, and chunking

data.title: Scaffold and build
data.code:
npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react-ts
cd my-app && npm install
npm run dev
npm run build && npm run preview

data.text: Only variables prefixed with `VITE_` are exposed to client code, and they are inlined at build time — never put secrets in them. Use `.env`, `.env.local` (git-ignored), and mode-specific files such as `.env.production`.

data.caption: Accessing and typing env variables

data.title: Build-time inlining
data.text: `import.meta.env` values are string-substituted into the bundle. A leaked API key is readable by anyone who downloads the JavaScript, no matter how it is named.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: Explain the unbundled dev server, the Rollup production build, and why `import.meta.env` is safe only for public values.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Vite serves native ESM in dev and bundles with Rollup for production.
esbuild handles fast per-file transforms during development.
Prefix public env vars with VITE_; they are inlined at build time.
Configure aliases and API proxies in vite.config.ts, not in app code.
data.takeaway: Vite is the default choice for new frontend apps — know why it starts faster than Webpack.
